column1: # iota(4,11) >= 32 ?  the deg(0) = 13 cube under cryptominisat5, over the
# FULL degree-sequence split, one line per sub-cube.  Second opinion for
# cadical's UNSAT at 85123.9 s (docs/ladder/iota4_11.tsv).
# Written by `iota_sym --checkpoint`; a row is appended the moment a
# sub-cube lands, so a reclaimed container loses only what was in flight.
# Resume with the same --checkpoint: UNSAT/SAT rows are skipped, UNKNOWN
# rows are re-run, because UNKNOWN is a budget and not a verdict.
# THE CUBE IS UNSAT ONLY WHEN ALL 1949 SUB-CUBES ARE UNSAT.  Note 1949,
# not the 1939 that docs/ladder/iota4_11.deg13.tsv states -- see the
# roadmap section for this session.  1939 is the count under
# `all_points_used = true`; the driver runs with it FALSE, and the ten
# extra sequences are the ones with a point of degree zero.
# Command:
#   iota_sym 4 11 32 --only-deg 13 --solver cryptominisat5 \
#     --seqprefix 11 --cubecap 2000 --slice 60 --seconds 600 --threads 4 \
#     --checkpoint docs/ladder/iota4_11.deg13.cryptominisat5.tsv
# Why the full split and not the prefix-3 split that roadmap 50.3 asked
# for: the prefix-3 split of this cube is 27 sub-cubes, and the four that
# were ever attempted (under cadical, iota4_11.deg13.p3.tsv) all burned
# 2400 s without landing.  Those four are the four LARGEST -- the
# enumeration is most-extreme-first -- covering 559, 327, 181 and 94 full
# sub-cubes respectively.  At the 136-491 s a full sub-cube costs, the
# largest prefix-3 cube is ~168000 s of search, so a 7200 s budget banks
# nothing and spends 28800 s learning that again.  The full split is what
# iota4_11.deg13.tsv calls the working granularity, and it is the only
# granularity at target 32 with measured evidence of landing.
# sub-cube
